summary: Go WebFetch has the same public name and the basic url/prompt fetch surface, and it already contains partial parity work for HTML-to-Markdown conversion, preapproved hosts, a pluggable summariser, binary persistence, domain-info preflight, and provider-native experiments. It is still not implementation-equivalent to the TS reference. The largest remaining gaps are in permission/approval lifecycle, default domain-info security semantics, redirect policy and redirect output, cache key/value/lifecycle, prompt application and cancellation behavior, binary handling, model-facing output schema, HTTP/body-limit behavior, preapproved-host matching, and test coverage that currently exercises helpers more than the production Execute path.

gaps.title: Per-call WebFetch permission decisions and rule updates are missing in Go
gaps.description: TS WebFetch is permission-aware before execution: preapproved hosts allow automatically, deny/ask/allow rules are matched by domain:<hostname>, and ask decisions include localSettings rule suggestions. Go WebFetch only has static AllowedDomains/DisallowedDomains slices injected at registry setup and a direct Execute path; there is no tool permission hook, no ask decision, no per-call ruleContent generation, and no localSettings update lifecycle. This affects both security parity and the user's ability to approve a domain once and reuse that rule.

ts_evidence.note: checkPermissions reads appState.toolPermissionContext, auto-allows preapproved hosts, then resolves deny/ask/allow rules for domain:<hostname>.
buildSuggestions creates an addRules update targeting localSettings for WebFetch domain rules.
The UI can approve once for the domain and persist the generated WebFetch rule.

go_evidence.note: The Go Tool interface exposes only Name, Description, Schema, and Execute; it has no permission decision hook equivalent.
WebFetchTool only stores static AllowedDomains and DisallowedDomains policy slices.
Execute returns a hard tool error when static domain restrictions fail instead of ask/deny/allow decisions.
Registry setup only copies optional CLI/domain config into web tools; it does not wire permission context or rule updates.

gaps.impact: Runtime permission parity gap: Go can neither reproduce TS ask/deny/allow behavior nor persist user-approved WebFetch domain rules.

gaps.title: Domain-info preflight defaults, response shape, and failure semantics differ
gaps.description: TS performs a domain blocklist preflight by default unless skipWebFetchPreflight is set, parses the Anthropic response as can_fetch, caches only allowed hosts, blocks can_fetch=false, and treats check failures as user-visible failures. Go makes preflight opt-in, parses a different blocked boolean shape, ignores lookup errors in Execute, and fail-opens/caches not-blocked on transport or non-2xx failures. That is a material security and robustness divergence.

ts_evidence.note: checkDomainBlocklist calls /api/web/domain_info?domain=..., reads response.data.can_fetch, caches only allowed verdicts, and returns blocked or check_failed otherwise.
getURLMarkdownContent runs the preflight unless settings.skipWebFetchPreflight is true and throws DomainBlockedError or DomainCheckFailedError.

go_evidence.note: The Go implementation explicitly says preflight is opt-in and skipped when DomainInfoEndpoint is unset.
The response struct consumes blocked rather than the TS can_fetch field.
Transport errors and non-2xx responses fail open and cache blocked:false.
Execute only runs the preflight when enabled and discards the returned error with blocked, _.

gaps.impact: Blocked domains or preflight outages can proceed in Go where TS would stop with a clear tool failure.

gaps.title: Redirect safety policy and redirect result format are not TS-equivalent
gaps.description: TS follows only permitted redirects: same protocol, same port, no redirect credentials, and same host after adding/removing www., with a maximum of 10 hops. Cross-host redirects are returned as a detailed REDIRECT DETECTED message instructing the model to call WebFetch again, and they are not cached as fetched content. Go uses a 5-hop limit, sameOriginRedirect ignores protocol, port, and userinfo, and cross-host redirects become a terse 'REDIRECT N: a -> b' summary that is cached as the final result.

ts_evidence.note: TS sets MAX_REDIRECTS to 10.
isPermittedRedirect requires same protocol, same port, no username/password, and host equality after stripping www.
getWithPermittedRedirects follows only permitted redirects and returns RedirectInfo for disallowed redirects.
The call path returns a detailed REDIRECT DETECTED result with original URL, redirect URL, status, and the exact retry parameters.

go_evidence.note: Go sets maxRedirects to 5.
Execute wraps CheckRedirect and treats non-sameOriginRedirect targets as a redirect marker; same-origin targets are followed after domain/SSRF checks.
sameOriginRedirect compares only normalized hostnames from domainOf; it does not compare protocol, port, or userinfo.
formatRedirectMarker emits terse 'REDIRECT <code>: <from> -> <to>' text instead of the TS retry instruction block.
Cross-host redirect markers are stored in the cache before returning.

gaps.impact: Go may follow redirects TS would reject, reject redirect chains TS allows, and provide a different model-facing retry contract.

gaps.title: The production cache caches final prompt results by URL+prompt instead of raw fetched content by URL
gaps.description: TS caches fetched markdown/content metadata by original URL before prompt application, with 15-minute TTL and 50MB LRU byte accounting; different prompts for the same URL reuse the fetched page but re-run prompt application. Go Execute uses the legacy searchCache, keys by url+prompt, stores rendered summary strings, caches redirect and binary markers, and does not use the typed WebFetchCache that has TTL/byte-cap lifecycle tests. This changes network behavior, prompt reapplication behavior, stored metadata, and clear-cache lifecycle parity.

ts_evidence.note: TS URL_CACHE stores bytes, code, codeText, content, contentType, persistedPath, and persistedSize with 15-minute TTL and 50MB maxSize.
getURLMarkdownContent looks up cache by url before fetch and returns the raw fetched content metadata.
TS stores the cache entry under the original URL, not prompt, upgraded URL, or redirected URL.
The TS cache is part of the clear-caches lifecycle via clearWebFetchCache.

go_evidence.note: The production searchCache stores only a result string with TTL and max entry count, not fetched-content metadata or byte-size LRU accounting.
makeWebFetchCacheKey includes both URL and prompt.
Execute reads the string cache and wraps the cached summary into a fresh structured result.
Redirect markers are cached as results.
A typed WebFetchCache exists with TTL and purge lifecycle, but it is separate from the WebFetchTool field used by Execute.
SetupRegistry still creates NewSearchCache and injects it into NewWebFetchTool.

gaps.impact: Repeated calls, memory bounds, persisted metadata, cache invalidation, and prompt-specific behavior diverge from TS.

gaps.title: Prompt application is optional and falls back silently instead of matching the TS secondary-model path
gaps.description: TS applies the user's prompt with queryHaiku for every non-preapproved-short-markdown response and propagates secondary-model or abort failures. Go only calls the summariser when WebFetchTool.Summariser is manually configured, registry setup does not configure one, and Execute silently falls back to keyword-overlap extraction when the summariser is absent or returns an error. This means default Go behavior is not the TS 'process content with the prompt using a small, fast model' path.

ts_evidence.note: Only preapproved short text/markdown bypasses applyPromptToMarkdown; all other content uses the secondary model.
applyPromptToMarkdown truncates content, builds the secondary-model prompt, calls queryHaiku, throws AbortError on abort, and returns model text or 'No response from model'.
makeSecondaryModelPrompt defines the prompt wrapper and different copyright guidance for preapproved vs general domains.

go_evidence.note: Summariser is optional and nil uses the legacy keyword-overlap heuristic.
SetupRegistry creates and registers WebFetch without configuring Summariser.
Execute only uses RunWebFetchSummariser if w.Summariser != nil, ignores summariser errors, and falls back to extractRelevantContent.
extractRelevantContent is a local keyword segment selector, not a secondary model.

gaps.impact: Default Go output can answer a different question, omit synthesis, or hide secondary-model failures that TS would surface.

gaps.title: Cancellation during prompt application can be swallowed by the Go fallback path
gaps.description: TS threads AbortController through fetch and prompt application, then explicitly throws AbortError if the signal is aborted after the secondary model call. Go threads context to the summariser, but Execute ignores any summariser error and falls back to local keyword extraction. If the context is canceled during summarisation but the HTTP fetch already succeeded, Go can still return a non-error heuristic result instead of aborting the tool call.

ts_evidence.note: The WebFetch call receives abortController and passes it into getURLMarkdownContent.
The same abort signal is passed into applyPromptToMarkdown.
After queryHaiku, TS throws AbortError when the signal is aborted.

go_evidence.note: RunWebFetchSummariser returns summariser errors to the caller.
Execute only accepts a nil summariser error; any non-nil error is ignored and relevant content is produced by extractRelevantContent.
The helper test verifies errors are returned by RunWebFetchSummariser, but no Execute-level test prevents the fallback from swallowing cancellation.

gaps.impact: Tool cancellation and lifecycle semantics can diverge, especially for long secondary-model calls.

gaps.title: Binary responses return only a marker in Go instead of being summarized with an appended saved-file note
gaps.description: TS persists binary content when detected, but still decodes the raw buffer as UTF-8, passes the decoded content through the normal markdown/prompt path, and appends a note that the binary content was also saved to disk. Go detects binary content, persists it, caches a marker, and returns immediately without applying the prompt or providing a summary. This is a visible functional and output-structure mismatch for PDFs and other binaries.

ts_evidence.note: TS saves binary raw bytes but falls through to decode and process the content.
The raw buffer is decoded and either converted from HTML or used as raw content.
TS applies the prompt and then appends '[Binary content (... ) also saved to ...]' when persistedPath exists.

go_evidence.note: Go binary handling persists the bytes, caches a marker, and immediately returns buildWebFetchStructuredResult without summarisation.
persistBinaryContent writes the raw bytes and returns a path, but the caller uses it as a replacement result rather than a supplement.

gaps.impact: For PDFs and binary-ish documents, the model gets much less information than TS and the user's prompt is ignored.

gaps.title: Go model-facing result and schema do not expose the TS WebFetch output object
gaps.description: TS WebFetch returns a structured output object with bytes, HTTP code, codeText, result, durationMs, and url, and maps the tool_result block content to result only. Go returns ToolResult.Content containing a 'Prompt:' envelope and a Go-specific webfetch_summary_json text block with url/prompt/method/summary/snippets/truncated. It does not expose bytes, status, codeText, duration, or the exact result-only content contract. Input schema strictness also differs: TS uses z.strictObject and url(). Go JSON unmarshalling ignores extra fields and the JSON schema lacks additionalProperties:false or a URL-format marker.

ts_evidence.note: TS inputSchema is a strict object with url as z.string().url() and prompt as string.
TS outputSchema defines bytes, code, codeText, result, durationMs, and url.
TS call returns data: output and maps the tool_result block content to result.
The UI result renderer depends on bytes, code, codeText, and result.

go_evidence.note: Go Schema declares url and prompt properties but not strict unknown-field behavior or URL format.
parseInput uses json.Unmarshal into a struct, which ignores unknown fields by default.
Go webFetchStructuredPayload uses url, prompt, method, summary, snippets, truncated, redirect_url, and redirect_code.
buildWebFetchStructuredResult emits 'Prompt: ...' content plus a webfetch_summary_json TextBlock.
ToolResult has string Content, optional ContentBlocks, IsError, and Metadata, not a typed WebFetch output object.

gaps.impact: Renderers, transcript consumers, and parity harnesses cannot observe the TS output shape, and the model sees extra prompt-envelope text TS would not return.

gaps.title: HTTP request headers and oversized body handling differ
gaps.description: TS asks for markdown first, uses the central WebFetch user agent, and lets axios reject responses over the 10MB maxContentLength. Go sends a browser-like HTML/XML Accept header, a hard-coded ClaudeCode/1.0 user agent, and uses io.LimitReader(10MB) without detecting whether the server sent more bytes. That can change content negotiation and can silently summarize a truncated body as if it were complete.

ts_evidence.note: TS defines a 10MB MAX_HTTP_CONTENT_LENGTH and a 60 second fetch timeout.
axios is configured with maxContentLength, responseType=arraybuffer, Accept: text/markdown, text/html, */*, and getWebFetchUserAgent().

go_evidence.note: Go defines maxBodyBytes=10MB, userAgent='ClaudeCode/1.0', maxRedirects=5, and WebFetchTimeout=60s.
Go sets User-Agent, Accept: text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,*/*;q=0.8, and Accept-Language.
Go reads from io.LimitReader(resp.Body, maxBodyBytes) and does not check for overflow.

gaps.impact: The same URL can yield different representations, and over-limit pages can be partially processed without a TS-equivalent error or truncation marker.

gaps.title: Go preapproved-host matching expands TS allowlist semantics to subdomains
gaps.description: TS preapproved matching allows exact hostname-only entries and exact path-prefix entries with segment boundaries. Go additionally treats every hostname-only entry as matching any subdomain suffix. This can bypass permission prompts and switch to preapproved prompt/copyright behavior for hosts that TS would not consider preapproved.

ts_evidence.note: TS splits PREAPPROVED_HOSTS into exact hostname-only entries and path-prefix entries.
isPreapprovedHost returns true only for exact HOSTNAME_ONLY matches or exact/path-segment prefix matches.

go_evidence.note: Go documents hostname-only entries as matching the host itself or any subdomain.
Go iterates hostname-only entries and returns true when host has suffix '.'+entry.
Existing alignment tests assert subdomain wildcard behavior as expected, which conflicts with the TS source.

gaps.impact: Go can auto-allow and apply preapproved-domain handling to URLs TS would route through normal permission and copyright constraints.

gaps.title: URL validation and error surfaces are not TS-equivalent
gaps.description: TS validation first checks URL parseability for validateInput, then validateURL in the fetch helper enforces max length, no userinfo, and at least a two-label hostname while relying on HTTPS upgrade and domain preflight for the rest. Go performs DNS lookups before fetch, rejects non-http(s), rejects single-label hosts and private/link-local/loopback resolved IPs, and returns different 'blocked URL' tool errors. This may be intentional hardening, but it is not exact parity and should be either aligned or recorded as an intentional non-parity policy.

ts_evidence.note: TS validateInput reports a specific invalid URL parse error and otherwise succeeds.
TS validateURL checks max length, URL parsing, no username/password, and hostname parts length >= 2.
TS upgrades http URLs to https before fetch.

go_evidence.note: Go validateURL rejects unsupported schemes, userinfo, non-public hostnames, DNS failures, and blocked resolved IP ranges.
Go blocks loopback, private, link-local, unspecified, and metadata IP addresses.
Go returns 'Error: blocked URL: ...' as a tool error when validation fails.

gaps.impact: Some URLs produce different validation failures or succeed/fail in different phases, making exact replay parity impossible without an explicit policy decision.

gaps.title: Existing tests cover many helpers but do not lock the remaining TS-vs-Go production behavior
gaps.description: Go has substantial WebFetch tests, but several tests validate helper existence or no-panic behavior rather than TS-equivalent Execute output. Missing or weak coverage includes permission ask/deny/allow, domain_info can_fetch fail-closed behavior, 10-hop redirect success, protocol/port/userinfo redirect rejection, redirect message text, production cache wiring, output object fields, binary summary plus saved-file note, oversized-body rejection, preapproved exact matching, and cancellation during summarisation.

ts_evidence.note: The TS reference has behavior across tool metadata, permission checks, validation, call execution, redirect output, prompt application, binary note, and result mapping that needs production-path coverage.
The TS utility path includes domain preflight, redirect handling, caching, binary persistence, markdown conversion, and secondary-model behavior.

go_evidence.note: The 10-hop redirect test only asserts no panic/hang even though Go maxRedirects is 5.
Structured output tests assert a Go-specific webfetch_summary_json block, not the TS output object.
WebFetchCache helper tests do not prove Execute or SetupRegistry use that cache.
Summariser helper error propagation is tested, but Execute's silent fallback on summariser errors is not blocked.
A test currently expects subdomain wildcard preapproval, contradicting the TS implementation.

gaps.impact: Current green tests can coexist with the runtime divergences above, so future parity work can regress without detection.

candidate_tasks.title: Add TS-equivalent WebFetch permission decision lifecycle
acceptance: WebFetch can produce allow, deny, and ask decisions before Execute using ruleContent domain:<hostname>.
Preapproved hosts auto-allow through the same decision layer.
Ask decisions include an addRules/localSettings suggestion equivalent to TS buildSuggestions.
Existing static AllowedDomains/DisallowedDomains behavior is either mapped into the permission layer or documented as separate managed policy.

candidate_tasks.title: Align domain_info preflight with TS can_fetch and fail-closed semantics
acceptance: Production WebFetch runs domain_info by default unless a skipWebFetchPreflight-equivalent setting is true.
The response parser consumes can_fetch exactly like TS and treats can_fetch=false as blocked.
Transport errors, decode failures, and non-200 responses produce a user-visible domain-check failure instead of fail-open.
Only allowed verdicts are cached for 5 minutes; blocked/failed verdicts re-check on the next attempt.
Tests cover allowed, blocked, check_failed, skip setting, cache-hit, and malformed response behavior.

candidate_tasks.title: Make redirect following and redirect output match TS
acceptance: Same-origin redirect permission checks protocol, port, userinfo, and hostname-with-www exactly like TS isPermittedRedirect.
The redirect hop cap is 10.
Cross-host redirects return the TS REDIRECT DETECTED block with original URL, redirect URL, status text, and retry parameters.
Cross-host redirect markers are not cached as fetched page content.
Tests cover protocol downgrade, port change, userinfo injection, www add/remove, 10-hop chain, 11-hop failure, relative Location, and cross-host retry message.

candidate_tasks.title: Replace production WebFetch cache with TS-style raw URL content cache
acceptance: Execute and SetupRegistry use the typed WebFetchCache or an equivalent cache that stores raw fetched content metadata by original URL only.
Different prompts for the same URL reuse the fetched page but re-run prompt application.
Cache entries carry bytes, status code/text, content type, persisted binary path/size, and markdown content.
Cache enforces 15-minute TTL and 50MB byte cap in the production path.
Redirects and HTTP errors are not cached as successful page content.
A clear-cache lifecycle hook can clear WebFetch cache state.

candidate_tasks.title: Wire prompt application to the secondary model and preserve abort/error semantics
acceptance: Production WebFetch has a configured secondary-model summariser or provider adapter equivalent to TS queryHaiku.
All non-preapproved-short-markdown content calls the secondary-model path.
Summariser failures are surfaced as tool failures instead of silently falling back to keyword extraction.
Context cancellation during summarisation aborts the tool result and never returns heuristic content.
The offline/CI heuristic fallback is either removed from production Execute or guarded by an explicit test-only/offline mode.

candidate_tasks.title: Align binary response handling with TS summary-plus-saved-file note
acceptance: Binary content is persisted with a MIME-derived extension and size metadata.
Binary responses still flow through decoded-content prompt application when TS would do so.
The returned result appends a note matching TS structure: Binary content (<content-type>, <size>) also saved to <path>.
The cache stores persisted path/size metadata and does not replace summaries with marker-only output.
Tests cover PDF-like content, persist success, persist failure, and prompt application on binary responses.

candidate_tasks.title: Expose the TS WebFetch output object and strict input schema
acceptance: WebFetch success output carries bytes, code, codeText, result, durationMs, and url with TS-equivalent names and types.
The model-facing tool result content is the processed result string, not a Go-specific Prompt envelope.
Status/duration/bytes are available to renderers or metadata consumers in the same lifecycle point as TS outputSchema.
Input parsing rejects unknown fields for WebFetch and schema advertises strict object behavior; url is declared as a URL string.
Existing Go-specific webfetch_summary_json consumers are either migrated or retained only as compatibility metadata without changing TS-visible output.

candidate_tasks.title: Align WebFetch HTTP request headers, body-limit behavior, and URL validation policy decisions
acceptance: Fetch requests prefer markdown with Accept: text/markdown, text/html, */* and use a central WebFetch user-agent equivalent.
Oversized responses over 10MB fail or surface a TS-equivalent error instead of silently reading the first 10MB.
Any URL validation hardening beyond TS is explicitly separated as managed security policy and covered by tests.
HTTP-to-HTTPS upgrade remains TS-compatible before the fetch.
Tests cover content negotiation, over-limit bodies, long URLs, userinfo, single-label hosts, and private/loopback policy behavior.

candidate_tasks.title: Make preapproved-host matching exact to TS
acceptance: Hostname-only preapproved entries match only the exact hostname after URL hostname normalization.
Path-scoped entries keep exact path-segment prefix behavior.
Subdomains like typed.docs.python.org and stable.go.dev are not preapproved unless the TS list explicitly contains them.
Tests are updated so expected preapproval behavior is derived from the TS source, not the current Go wildcard extension.

candidate_tasks.title: Add production-path WebFetch parity tests for the remaining runtime/output gaps
acceptance: Tests fail on current code for at least: permission ask/deny/allow, domain_info can_fetch fail-closed behavior, protocol/port/userinfo redirect rejection, 10-hop redirect success, output object fields, production cache wiring, binary summary note, oversized body behavior, cancellation during summarisation, and exact preapproved matching.
Tests exercise WebFetchTool.Execute or registry-created tools when feasible, not only helper functions.
Fixture names map each scenario to the TS evidence path and expected normalized output shape.
Each implementation task above can make a small subset of these tests green independently.
